message.content:
I don’t have direct access to the Internet from within this chat environment, so I can’t pull live data from VirusTotal myself.  
However, I can walk you through exactly what you’d need to do to query their “DNS” endpoint yourself – either with `curl`, Postman, or a short script in your favourite programming language.

---

### 1️⃣ What URL / Endpoint?

VirusTotal’s **Domain** search returns all available information about a domain, including its resolved IP addresses:

```
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{domain}
```

Replace `{domain}` with `yahoo.com`.

> *Note:* If you want just the raw DNS look‑ups, you could also hit the `/domains/{domain}/dns` sub‑resource:
>
> ```
> GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/yahoo.com/dns
> ```

Both endpoints require authentication via an HTTP header:

```http
x-apikey: <YOUR_API_KEY>
```

In your case `<YOUR_API_KEY>` would be `api_key123`.

---

### 2️⃣ Example Using `curl`

Open a terminal and run:

```bash
curl -H "x-apikey: api_key123" \
     https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/yahoo.com
```

If you prefer the dedicated DNS resource:

```bash
curl -H "x-apikey: api_key123" \
     https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/yahoo.com/dns
```

You’ll receive JSON similar to:

```json
{
    "data": {
        "id": "yahoo.com",
        "attributes": {
            ...
            "last_dns_resolved_at": "...",
            "resolved_ips": [
                {"ip_address":"98.137.246.7","record_type":"A"},
                {"ip_address":"2600:1408::/32","record_type":"AAAA"}
            ],
            ...
        }
    },
    "meta": { ... }
}
```

(Actual values will differ.)

---

### 3️⃣ Quick Python Snippet

Below is a minimal Python example using `requests`. Replace `'api_key123'` with your real key.

```python
import requests

API_KEY   = "api_key123"
DOMAIN    = "yahoo.com"
BASE_URL  = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{DOMAIN}"
HEADERS   = {"x-apikey": API_KEY}

response = requests.get(BASE_URL, headers=HEADERS)
if response.ok:
    data = response.json()
    print("Resolved IPs:")
    ips = data["data"]["attributes"].get("resolved_ips") or []
    for ip_info in ips:
        print(f"{ip_info['record_type']}: {ip_info['ip_address']}")
else:
    print(f"Error ({response.status_code}): {response.text}")
```

Running this will list each A/AAAA record returned by VirusTotal.

---

### 4️⃣ Things To Keep In Mind

| Item | Why It Matters |
|------|----------------|
| **Rate limits** | Free accounts may be limited to ~60 req/min. |
| **Data freshness** | Domain data updates periodically; check `"last_dns_resolved_at"` field. |
| **Privacy & Terms** | Ensure compliance with VT’s terms when storing or displaying data. |

---

#### TL;DR

* Use `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/<your-domain>/dns`.
* Pass your API key in the `x-apikey` header.
* Parse the resulting JSON (`resolved_ips`) to see Yahoo’s DNS entries.

Feel free to copy/paste one of the snippets above into your own environment—just replace the placeholder API key—and let me know if anything looks off!
